## Overview

This vignette demonstrates the end-to-end haploStack workflow starting from
**PLINK 1.9 PED/MAP** files.  The same pipeline applies to any ploidy level —
ploidy is inferred automatically from the number of allele columns in the PED
file.

```
Input files                Output artefacts
───────────────────────    ──────────────────────────────────────────
my_genotype.ped            GenoMeta object (in memory)
my_genotype.map            Haplotype profile (.rds)
my_blocks.txt              Block location table (.csv)
my_effects_yield.txt       Local-GEBV matrix (.txt per trait)
                           Format-converted genotype files (.ped / .csv)
                           Plots (Manhattan, block-counts, alignment)
```

---

## 1  Input file formats

### 1.1  PED file (`.ped`)

Standard PLINK 1.9 PED — space-delimited, no header:

```
FID   IID   Father  Mother  Sex  Phenotype  A1_M1  A2_M1  A1_M2  A2_M2 ...
FAM1  S001  0       0       0    -9         A      T      G      G     ...
FAM1  S002  0       0       0    -9         A      A      G      C     ...
```

Each marker occupies two consecutive columns (one per allele).  The ploidy
is detected from `(ncol - 6) / n_markers`.

### 1.2  MAP file (`.map`)

Standard PLINK 4-column MAP — no header:

```
Chrom   Marker    cM    Pos_bp
1H      SNP_001   0     12340000
1H      SNP_002   0     18920000
```

### 1.3  Block file (optional, `.txt`)

Either **coordinate format** (Chrom, Block, Start, End) or
**marker-level format** (Chrom, Marker, Block) — tab-delimited with header.
If omitted you can attach block information later via `attach_block_info()`.

### 1.4  Effect file (one per trait, `.txt`)

Three columns — no header required:

```
Marker    Allele  Effect
SNP_001   A       0.0412
SNP_002   G      -0.0187
```

---

## 2  Read genotype data

```{r read-plink}
library(haploStack)
library(data.table)

# ── Read PED + MAP (and optionally a block file) ──────────────────────────────
meta <- read_plink_ped(
  ped_file   = "data/my_genotype.ped",
  map_file   = "data/my_genotype.map",
  block_file = "data/my_blocks.txt",   # omit if attaching blocks separately
  pos_unit   = "bp"                    # or "mbp" if positions are in megabase-pairs
)

is_geno_meta(meta)   # TRUE

cat("Samples :", meta$metadata$n_samples,  "\n")
cat("Markers :", meta$metadata$n_markers,  "\n")
cat("Ploidy  :", meta$metadata$ploidy,     "\n")
cat("Encoding:", names(meta$metadata$char_dict), "\n")

# Inspect the array — dim order is (n_samples, n_markers, ploidy)
dim(meta$geno_arrays)
head(meta$map_info)
```

---

## 3  Attach block information (if not loaded with the reader)

Skip this step if you passed `block_file` to `read_plink_ped()` above.

```{r attach-blocks}
# From a marker-level block-map data.frame (Chrom, Marker, Block)
block_map <- fread("data/my_blocks.txt")

meta <- attach_block_info(meta, block_source = block_map)

# Confirm blocks attached
head(meta$block_marker_map_info)
nrow(meta$block_info)
```

---

## 4  Build block location table

`build_block_location_info()` summarises each block's chromosomal span,
midpoint, and SNP count.  It can also write a CSV directly.

```{r block-location}
bloc <- build_block_location_info(
  meta,
  output_dir = "output",      # set NULL to skip writing
  prefix     = "barley_ped"
)

# bloc$block_info  — data.table: Chrom, Block, Start, End, Pos, Num_SNPs, Block_length
print(bloc$block_info)
```

---

## 5  Create haplotype profile

`GenoMeta` is the central object: it stores the genotype array, map, block
assignments, and `sample_info`. The per-haplotype allele table and marker/block
metadata are derived on demand with `geno_meta_views()`.

```{r profile}
profile <- geno_meta_views(meta)

cat("Encoding :", profile$encoding,              "\n")
cat("Samples  :", length(profile$samples),       "\n")
cat("Blocks   :", nrow(profile$block_meta),      "\n")
cat("Markers  :", nrow(profile$marker_meta),     "\n")

# Allele table — rows: samples × ploidy, cols: markers
head(profile$alleles[, 1:8, with = FALSE])

# Save the GenoMeta for later use
save_geno_meta(meta, "output/barley_ped_geno_meta.rds")
```

---

## 6  Compute local GEBVs

Local GEBVs measure the haplotype-block-level contribution to a trait.
One effect file per trait; use a named list for multi-trait analysis.

```{r effects}
# ── Single trait ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
eff_yield <- read_effect_file("data/effects_yield.txt")

gebv_yield <- compute_profile_localgebv(
  profile        = profile,
  effect_df      = eff_yield,
  level          = "genotype",   # "haplotype" for per-haplotype values
  center = "allele_freq"
)

# Wide data.table: Block column + one column per sample
cat("GEBV matrix:", dim(gebv_yield), "(blocks × samples + 1)\n")
print(gebv_yield[1:5, 1:6, with = FALSE])

# Save GEBV matrix
fwrite(gebv_yield, "output/gebv_yield.txt", sep = "\t")
```

---

## 7  Run the full catalogue (multi-trait)

`run_haplotype_catalogue()` wraps the profile, GEBV calculation, and plot
generation into a single call.

```{r catalogue}
effect_list <- list(
  Yield    = read_effect_file("data/effects_yield.txt"),
  Protein  = read_effect_file("data/effects_protein.txt"),
  Maturity = read_effect_file("data/effects_maturity.txt")
)

results <- run_haplotype_catalogue(
  geno_meta      = meta,
  effect_list    = effect_list,
  output_dir     = "output/catalogue_plink",
  ld_threshold   = 0.5,
  save_profile   = TRUE,        # writes output/catalogue_plink/haplotype_profile_*.rds
  center = "allele_freq",
  n_cores        = 1L           # set > 1 (requires future + future.apply) for parallel
)

# Per-trait named list: gebv_matrix, gebv_summary, block_counts, profile
names(results)
names(results$Yield)
```

The following files are written to `output/catalogue_plink/`:

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `haplotype_profile_0.5_t0.rds` | Serialised haplotype profile |
| `Haplotype_GA_Matrix_*_Yield.txt` | Block × Sample GEBV matrix |
| `GEBV_*_Yield.txt` | Per-sample total GEBV |
| `Block_Counts_*_Yield.txt` | Positive / zero / negative block counts |
| `Manhattan_Variance_*_Yield.png` | Manhattan plot of effect variance |
| `Manhattan_Effect_*_Yield.png` | Manhattan plot of per-sample effects |
| `Block_Counts_Yield.png` | Stacked bar chart of block counts |

---

## 8  Visualise results

Plots are produced automatically by `run_haplotype_catalogue()`, but you can
regenerate or customise them directly.

```{r plots, eval=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
library(ggplot2)

# ── Manhattan — effect variance ───────────────────────────────────────────────
block_var <- results$Yield$gebv_matrix |>
  data.table::melt(id.vars = "Block", variable.name = "Sample",
                   value.name = "Effect") |>
  merge(bloc$block_info[, .(Block, Chrom, Pos)], by = "Block") |>
  (\(dt) dt[, .(BlockVariance = var(Effect, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(Block, Chrom, Pos)])()

p_var <- plot_manhattan_variance(block_var, trait_name = "Yield")
print(p_var)
ggsave("output/Manhattan_Variance_Yield.png", p_var, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 150)

# ── Block counts per sample ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
p_counts <- plot_block_counts(results$Yield$block_counts, trait_name = "Yield")
print(p_counts)
ggsave("output/Block_Counts_Yield.png", p_counts, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 150)

# ── Haplotype alignment (first 6 blocks) ─────────────────────────────────────
sub_meta <- filter_geno_meta(meta, blocks = profile$block_meta$block_id[1:6])
p_align  <- plot_haplotype_alignment(sub_meta, show_block_boundaries = TRUE)
print(p_align)
ggsave("output/Alignment_chr1.png", p_align, width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 150)
```

---

## 9  Filter the GenoMeta

Subset to a chromosome region, specific samples, or blocks of interest.

```{r filter}
# ── Keep chromosome 1H only ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
meta_1H <- filter_geno_meta(
  meta,
  chromosomes = list(list(chr = "1H"))
)

# ── Keep a selection of samples ───────────────────────────────────────────────
elite_names <- c("S001", "S002", "S010", "S011")
meta_elite  <- filter_geno_meta(meta, keep_samples = elite_names)
prof_elite  <- geno_meta_views(meta_elite)

cat("Elite subset: ", length(prof_elite$samples), "samples,",
    nrow(prof_elite$block_meta), "blocks\n")
```

---

## 10  Export genotypes in other formats

The GenoMeta object can be written out in SelectionTools (ST) or
genomicSimulation (GS) format for use in downstream tools, or back
to PLINK PED for QC checks.

```{r export}
# ── PLINK PED → SelectionTools CSV ───────────────────────────────────────────
# (the SelectionTools layout is behind use_st_formats(); st_formats = TRUE for one call)
write_geno_meta(meta, path = "output/genotype_st.csv", preset = "ST",
                st_formats = TRUE)

# ── PLINK PED → genomicSimulation CSV ────────────────────────────────────────
write_geno_meta(meta, path = "output/genotype_gs.csv", preset = "GS")

# ── Inspect the converted matrix without writing ─────────────────────────────
converted <- geno_meta_to_matrix(meta, preset = "ST", st_formats = TRUE)
# converted$matrix — markers as rows, samples as columns, "A/T" style cells
dim(converted$matrix)
converted$matrix[1:4, 1:5]

# ── Round-trip check: write back to PED ──────────────────────────────────────
write_geno_meta(meta, path = "output/genotype_roundtrip", preset = "PL")
# Writes: output/genotype_roundtrip.ped + output/genotype_roundtrip.map
```

---

## 11  Load a saved GenoMeta in a new session

```{r reload}
# In a new session — no need to reload raw genotype files
meta2 <- load_geno_meta("output/barley_ped_geno_meta.rds")
is_geno_meta(meta2)       # TRUE
meta2$metadata$encoding   # same encoding as saved
nrow(meta2$sample_info)
```
